candidates: When TypeScript errors appear in type-conversion utilities (e.g., `convert.ts`), fix the root cause by correcting the type definitions in `types.ts` to accurately reflect all values that can appear at runtime; use typed type-guard functions to narrow discriminated unions, and remove any `@ts-expect-error` suppressions or type casts rather than working around the type system. A type bug discovered in a `@ts-expect-error` code path is a strong signal that the suppression is masking a real problem.

When narrowing a `TSType` discriminated-union variant by its `name` string, also investigate whether a *structural* property unique to that variant (e.g., the presence or absence of `raw`, or the shape of `value`) can serve as a more robust discriminant; verify that the chosen structural property is consistent across all runtime inputs before relying on it as a type guard.

When an array property was previously typed as optional (`prop?: T[]`) and is being tightened to required (`prop: T[]`), confirm that all runtime code paths that construct or pass that object guarantee the property is present before calling array methods (`.filter()`, `.map()`, etc.) directly on it without optional chaining.
